description: Deterministic process checks for the hawkscan skill. Each check maps to a required behavior in SKILL.md. Harnesses should look for these signals in agent traces, command histories, or output text.

checks.description: Agent verifies the hawk CLI is installed and meets the minimum version (6.0.0) before proceeding.
checks.failure_guidance: If hawk < 6.0.0, the agent must stop and tell the user to upgrade. Proceeding risks using stale inline auth recipes instead of 'hawk config show'.

checks.description: Agent confirms the 'hawk config' subcommand is available (required for Phase 1c auth recipes).
checks.failure_guidance: hawk config show is the only source of canonical auth recipes. If unavailable, Phase 1c is not recoverable — agent must stop.

checks.description: Agent queries existing apps before creating one, to avoid duplicate application records.
checks.failure_guidance: Skipping this check and blindly creating a new app pollutes the org with duplicates and splits scan history.

checks.description: Agent queries existing environments before creating one.
checks.failure_guidance: Duplicate environments split finding history and break scan-to-scan comparison.

checks.description: Agent verifies hawk credentials exist (~/.hawk/hawk.properties) or runs hawk init before scanning.
checks.failure_guidance: Scanning without credentials fails with 401. Better to verify credentials early and fail fast.

checks.description: Agent confirms the application is running and reachable before attempting to scan.
checks.failure_guidance: HawkScan requires a live target. Scanning a non-running app exits with code 1 (connection error), not useful findings.

checks.description: Agent establishes an understanding of the target before configuring: how it runs locally, how to reach its API, whether it is a SPA, and whether it requires auth — by reading repo docs, exploring, or asking the user (not by running a fixed set of detection commands).
checks.failure_guidance: Generating config without understanding the app's run command, API style, SPA status, and auth need produces a mis-targeted or unauthenticated scan that returns few useful findings. The agent may determine these by reading AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/README, exploring the repo, or asking the user.

checks.description: stackhawk.yml uses ${VAR:default} env var interpolation for host, applicationId, and credentials — no hardcoded values.
checks.failure_guidance: Hardcoded values break multi-environment use and risk committing credentials to source control. In observe mode this check applies to generated YAML shown in agent output.

checks.description: stackhawk.yml does NOT use interpolation mid-string (e.g. host: "https://${HOST}/api" silently fails — the entire value must be the variable).
checks.failure_guidance: HawkScan only interpolates when the entire YAML value is the variable reference. Partial interpolation silently produces a broken URL.

checks.description: Agent does NOT create stackhawk.local.yml.
checks.failure_guidance: stackhawk.local.yml is an anti-pattern. Host overrides belong in ${APP_HOST:default} interpolation within the primary stackhawk.yml.

checks.description: Agent runs 'hawk validate config stackhawk.yml' (no -c flag, no absolute path) before scanning.
checks.failure_guidance: Config validation catches errors without burning a full scan run. The -c/--config flags do not exist and will cause the command to fail.

checks.description: If an authentication: block exists in stackhawk.yml, agent runs 'hawk validate auth stackhawk.yml' before scanning.
checks.failure_guidance: Skipping auth validation means auth failures surface mid-scan instead of in seconds. Mandatory when auth block is present.

checks.description: hawk scan and hawk rescan are run synchronously — never backgrounded with & or nohup.
checks.failure_guidance: Background scanning prevents reading the exit code. Exit code 42 (findings found) will be silently missed.

checks.description: hawk scan is invoked with --json-output for structured findings parsing.
checks.failure_guidance: Without --json-output, findings must be parsed from terminal stdout which is fragile. Use --json-output when hawk >= 5.3.41.

checks.description: COMMIT_SHA and BRANCH_NAME env vars are exported before scanning so scan results are traceable to the commit.
checks.failure_guidance: Without commit tagging, scan results can't be linked to the code change. Required for traceability in CI.

checks.description: HAWK_AGENT env var is detected and exported before scanning (populates the _STACKHAWK_AGENT tag).
checks.failure_guidance: HAWK_AGENT populates the _STACKHAWK_AGENT tag for agent attribution in the StackHawk platform. Missing = 'none'.

checks.description: hawk validate and hawk scan commands use bare filenames, not absolute paths.
checks.failure_guidance: The hawk CLI prepends the working directory to config paths. Absolute paths produce broken double-paths that cause the command to fail.

checks.description: Before routing findings to the fix loop, agent checks per-path triage status and skips FALSE_POSITIVE and RISK_ACCEPTED paths. Only applicable after a scan completes with findings.
checks.failure_guidance: Routing FALSE_POSITIVE findings to the fix loop creates churn against deliberate human decisions. This check only fires in full-auto mode with real scan results.

checks.description: After fixing findings, agent uses 'hawk rescan --scan-id' rather than launching a new full 'hawk scan', unless a documented full-scan condition applies.
checks.failure_guidance: hawk rescan re-runs only the plugins that fired on the parent scan — faster than a full scan. Use full scan only if new endpoints were added or codebase changed substantially.

checks.description: Agent never refers to the scanner as 'ZAP' or 'OWASP ZAP'.
checks.failure_guidance: The product is HawkScan (CLI/runtime) and StackHawk (platform). The underlying engine is HSTE. ZAP references are inaccurate and confusing to users.

checks.description: No API keys or credentials appear hardcoded in stackhawk.yml or commands.
checks.failure_guidance: Hardcoded API keys in stackhawk.yml will be committed to source control. Always use ${HAWK_API_KEY} interpolation.

checks.description: hawk validate and hawk scan commands do NOT use -c or --config flags (these flags don't exist).
checks.failure_guidance: The -c and --config flags do not exist in the hawk CLI. Inventing them causes the command to fail silently or with a confusing error.

checks.description: Agent read the repo's own docs (README/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING/docs).
checks.failure_guidance: Docs-first discovery orients from what the repo says before exploring.

checks.description: Agent inspected a build/manifest/API-defining file.
checks.failure_guidance: Manifests are where technology/API-style are definitively determined.

checks.description: Agent did NOT fall back to the old rigid grep/node detection checklist.
checks.failure_guidance: The docs-first rewrite replaced the rote command menu; falling back to it is a regression.

checks.description: The read-only guard denied nothing (no writes/scans/app-start/remote push).
checks.failure_guidance: Discovery is observational; any guard denial means the agent acted outside scope.

checks.description: For the base-path-mismatch scenario, the agent names the base/context-path resolution gap (the gate's base-path-mismatch signal) as the cause of the systematic 404s.
checks.failure_guidance: A spec whose paths all 404 while a prefixed variant resolves is a base-path/context-path mismatch, not a missing spec or an environment problem. Naming it correctly is what routes to the right fix (align app.host and the spec base path).

checks.description: For the auth-wall scenario, the agent names the auth-wall signal (authenticated paths returning a wall of 401/403) rather than misreading it as an environment problem or coverage-only.
checks.failure_guidance: A cluster of 401/403 across authenticated paths on a reachable app is a config-class auth-wall, fixed by correcting the authentication block — not an environment-class gap.

checks.description: For the auth-wall scenario, the agent reports the coverage evidence (routes reached vs. expected) rather than ignoring the under-coverage.
checks.failure_guidance: Coverage is evidence-only but must still be reported (e.g. 22 of 254 routes reached) so the gap is specific.

checks.description: The agent does NOT declare the scan done or the app secure while a gate gap is open.
anti_patterns: scan is complete and the app is secure
checks.failure_guidance: The gate reporting rule forbids claiming the scan is done or the app secure while a config- or environment-class gap remains open.
